result.text:
All 29 tests pass unchanged, and the image is saved.

## What I did

**Replaced the identification IFs with a polymorphic hierarchy** (`Identification` ← `DNI`, `CUIT`):
- `Identification class >> ofType:number:` finds the type with `typeFor:`, which detects among `self subclasses` the one whose `typeCode` matches (`'D'`/`'C'`), signalling `InvalidTypeError` when none does — the same `subclasses detect:` idiom the existing `Environment class >> current` already uses.
- The instance-creation funnel `number:` lives once in the abstract class: it runs `assertIsValidNumber:` and sends the only `initialize`. Each subclass supplies just `isValidNumber:` and its error description, so the DNI/CUIT validations no longer repeat the "check then `self error:`" scaffolding.
- `Customer` now holds an `identification` and delegates: `hasDNIAsIdentification` → `identification isDNI`, `dniNumberIfNone:` → `identification dniNumberIfNone:`, etc. No conditional survives in `Customer`.

**Same treatment for zip codes** (`ZipCode` ← `OldZipCode`, `NewZipCode`), dispatching on `canRepresent:` (first character digit vs. letter). `codeFrom:` is polymorphic too, so `OldZipCode` keeps an Integer and `NewZipCode` a String without an IF. A new zip code's four middle digits are validated by asking `OldZipCode isValidCode:` — the duplicated "4 digits, greater than 999" rule now exists in one place.

**Other repetition removed:** `String >> isAllDigits` / `isAllLetters` (the `allSatisfy: [:c | c isDigit]` block appeared five times); the shared `'Invalid identification type'` text now lives once in `InvalidTypeError`; the identical customer-lookup block duplicated in `TransientCustomerSystem` and `PersistentCustomerSystem` became `Customer >> isIdentifiedWithType:number:`.

**Collateral clean-up:** `Customer` and `Address` are now created complete (`named:lastNamed:identifiedBy:`, `at:number:town:zipCode:province:`) instead of `new` plus setters, so `importCustomer`/`importAddress` are five declarative lines each; the `newCustomer ifNil:` check became a `NoCustomerImported` null object (which owns the error text `CustomerImporter` still publishes for the test); `value` loops on `atEnd` instead of testing `nextLine` for nil; `record isEmpty ifTrue:` became `ifEmpty:`.

**What I deliberately left alone:** the `isCustomerRecord` / `isAddressRecord` dispatch in `importRecord` and the `isKindOf: Customer` check in `DataBaseSession >> persist:`. Both are pre-existing code outside the type explosion the exam describes, and polymorphizing the record dispatch would mean a whole record hierarchy for a two-branch guard. Say the word if you want those converted as well.

Tests were not modified; `ImportTest` was moved to the category `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial-Tests` as requested. I also exercised `PersistentCustomerSystem` manually (the tests only run the transient one) to confirm persistence and address id assignment still work.
